defects.title: Every read path opens the database READ-WRITE and writes the index
defects.observed: scope=orphaned created a 65,952-byte WAL; scope=all 98,912 bytes; history 107,152 bytes; the fixture db grew 643,072 → 704,512 bytes across the reads. On the T2 copy the default read-write open took 12,234.02ms against 19.31ms for a byte-read-only open, and the open moved the WAL 494,432 → 527,392 bytes (indexWriteFromReadWriteOpen=true).
defects.impact: A read tool mutates the index (Lead ruling B6) and pays 12.2s of migration/healer work on T2 before its first query. Fixing this also removes most of the T2 open latency.
defects.fixPlan: handler/engines open BrainDatabase.getRawInstance(projectId,{readonly:true}); history storage stays a separate concern (P-12).

defects.title: An unindexed project answers a clean-looking zero instead of refusing (library/CLI door) and a database is created
defects.observed: Against a directory the indexer never ran over, the source handler returned isError:false, 'patterns (0 found):\n  none\n[scan: 0 finding(s) ...]' — and created brain.db (4,096 bytes, schema later). The MCP stdio door refuses the same project ('No index found ... Run: bb index', isError true) because the server gate runs first; the CLI door and library callers have no gate.
defects.impact: A caller cannot distinguish 'nothing is dead' from 'there is no index'. The engine's own comment names this class: 'A crash and a clean result are indistinguishable if the corpus is not asserted real first.'
defects.fixPlan: the read-only open (P-01) throws the loud missing-index error; the handler returns it as isError text; CLI inherits the refusal.

defects.title: Default-call latency exceeds the campaign budget on T1 and T2, and a cold T2 scan is 133s
defects.observed: T2 default-all p50 19,839ms / p95 93,078ms (budget 5,000ms p95); T2 orphaned p50 20,424ms; T1 default-all p50 1,294ms / p95 1,749ms (budget 1000ms); cold detectOrphans on T2 133,520ms; warm-in-process handler 26,430ms. Load average 21-28 on 8 cores (declared; p50 cited).
defects.impact: At 4x the budget and within a bad-contention outlier of the 30s MCP client timeout; a cold first call can exceed it outright.
defects.fixPlan: read-only open removes 12.2s; then profile the six relationship statements on T2 (json_extract the suspect) and reduce warm-path work to the census aggregates the page needs.

defects.title: The handler's displayed page violates the requested-class representation contract the engine implements
defects.observed: On a fixture with 130 orphan candidates, 60 god classes and one framework row, the documented default {} returned 20 god-class rows and ZERO orphan rows and ZERO framework rows, while its own census line reported orphaned_function=855 orphaned_file=135 framework-detected=1. The engine's display page at maxResults=100 DID contain 38 orphan rows and the framework row; the handler asks the engine for max(limit,100) and then slices the top `limit`, so the promotion the engine applies to its page is discarded. limit=100 shows all three classes.
defects.impact: includeOrphaned/includeFramework default to true but a default call can return none of them on a real repository; an agent cannot distinguish 'no orphans' from 'page full of anti-patterns'.
defects.fixPlan: pass the caller's page size to the engine (or re-apply the one-slot-per-requested-class rule on the handler's slice) and keep the census unchanged; add a handler-level gate case that asserts representation at limit=20.

defects.title: history returns an unbounded findings payload in one answer
defects.observed: After one recorded run over 1,113 findings, {history:true,limit:2} returned 1,787,433 characters (1.79MB). `limit` bounds RUNS only; the findings array is loaded whole by the shared history reader; the answer is JSON with no truncation declaration. On T2's census (13,237 findings per run) one run alone is ~21MB, multiplied by recorded runs.
defects.impact: An MCP host receives a multi-megabyte tool answer; a 30s/timeout-bounded client can be starved by a history query that is not bounded at all.
defects.fixPlan: declare and enforce a findings window (or omit findings unless requested), name the bound and the total, and test a >window history.

defects.title: recordRun is silently ignored in scope=orphaned
defects.observed: {scope:'orphaned',recordRun:true} wrote no analysis run (runs 0 → 0, no error, no notice); the descriptor documents recordRun without a scope caveat.
defects.impact: A caller that asks to persist an orphan scan gets an unpersisted answer that reads as recorded.
defects.fixPlan: either record in both scopes or refuse scope=orphaned+recordRun by name and document it.

defects.title: limit has no upper bound and no declared maximum
defects.observed: limit=1,000,000,000 passed the boundary and returned all 1,113 rows / 55,402 characters on the fixture. The schema states no maximum and the descriptor's prose states a default only. The staleness resolver builds a `relative_path IN (?,?,..)` list from the page, so a page above SQLite's variable cap fails rather than truncating.
defects.impact: A caller can turn a bounded page into a multi-MB answer (T2 census 13,237) and, at a large enough limit, into an SQLite 'too many SQL variables' error instead of a declared bound.
defects.fixPlan: declare minimum/maximum in the schema, enforce a named refusal above the maximum in the handler, and state the census/raise-limit path in the error.

defects.title: Staleness remediation text promises auto-refresh and a refresh=false option the tool does not have
defects.observed: The live answer footer says 'reads auto-refresh stale files within budget when enabled — disable with BB_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1 or refresh=false; manual repair: run: bb index --changed'. The handler never calls maybeAutoRefresh and the schema has no `refresh` option; the generated page repeats the same sentence. The handler imports maybeAutoRefresh/autoRefreshLine/FRESHNESS_REMEDIATION_MANUAL_ONLY but uses none of them.
defects.impact: A caller told to disable a non-existent option, and told the tool repairs what it only reports.
defects.fixPlan: handler renders the manual-only remediation from the summary it already computes; generator needs a bb_patterns branch (like bb_visualize's) that states 'does not auto-refresh, no refresh option' — Lead-owned file, requested.

defects.title: Docs/curation describe engine-report fields the wire never carries
defects.observed: Curation: 'Every finding is confidence-qualified, carries an evidence array naming what was checked, and carries a limitations array ... summary.suppressedByReason ... summary.importResolution'. The tool answer is text: no per-finding evidence or limitations arrays, and neither unverifiedUsageEdges nor importResolution is rendered. What IS rendered: location, rule, confidence, [stale], census/per-rule counts, suppression counts (orphaned scope), provenance counts. The engine report carries the rest; the tool surface does not.
defects.impact: A reader of the tool page expects disclosures the tool call cannot show. Honest docs must separate engine-report semantics from the answer, or the text answer must render the missing summary lines.
defects.fixPlan: render the two aggregate disclosure lines the engine already computed (refused usage evidence; import resolution) in scope=orphaned, and rewrite the evidence-semantics text to say exactly where each field appears (text summary vs engine report).

defects.title: Per-tool gates have stale split assumptions and cannot fail/blend refusal text into a pass
defects.observed: m15-deep exits 2: it reads src/mcp/tool-registry.ts and splits on 'name: "bb_patterns"', which the split registry no longer contains. m13-docs fails 5: the description is read from doc line 3 (now the author header), the handler body is read from the 39-line assembler src/mcp/tool-handlers.ts, and freshness is checked by running the FULL generator (expected red mid-flight on shared artifacts). m13-contract/e2e MCP legs spawn StdioClientTransport without env, so BB_DATA_DIR never reaches the child: 4 failures read 'No index found'. Worse, three e2e MCP checks PASS on that refusal text ('output contains patterns' matches the temp path 'bb-patterns-mcp-...'; 'called function NOT flagged' passes because an error names no function) — a gate passing on its own refusal.
defects.impact: The three red gates cannot go green on the split tree, and the e2e gate can go green while measuring nothing.
defects.fixPlan: resolve code through script/lib/tool-sources.ts, parse the header-aware page, use --only bb_patterns for freshness, forward env to the stdio child, and make every transport check first assert isError:false before reading text.

defects.title: Source-fingerprint evidence list is stale after the split, so 'known-gap' integrity checks watch the wrong file
defects.observed: PATTERN_EVIDENCE_PATHS lists src/mcp/tool-handlers.ts (now a 39-line assembler) and omits src/mcp/tools/bb_patterns/handler.ts / descriptor.ts. patternSourceFingerprint therefore cannot change when the tool code changes, and patternRelevantWorkingTreeChanges (used for the m20 P2/P3 status field) reports [] while the handler is modified.
defects.impact: A committed 'verified' m20 receipt can be produced over changed tool code — the exact defect class the Lead's ruling 5 names.
defects.fixPlan: point the list at the split files; add a gate assertion that every path exists and that the list covers the handler/descriptor (red on a planted stale entry).

defects.title: The history read creates analysis-history schema through a shared read-write open
defects.observed: {history:true} on a fresh data dir moved the WAL by 107,152 bytes; ensureHistorySchema runs CREATE TABLE on the read path. Using the shared engine, the handler cannot avoid it by choosing a read-only handle.
defects.impact: Read path writes schema (Lead ruling B6) on a call the caller did not ask to persist anything.
defects.fixPlan: cross-scope request: run-history must open byte-read-only for reads and surface a loud 'no analysis history yet' answer instead of creating the table; handler then returns that answer.

defects.title: Curated guide is not owner-authored reference for this checkout: no §8 header, external corpus suite absent, a non-existent option, milestone/lane narrative, and one docs-truth claim is red
defects.observed: No author header. Lines 8-16 claim the harness and raw outputs are in bb_tests/bb_patterns/, which does not exist in this checkout (~/bb_tests has no bb_patterns directory) — every number in the page is therefore unreproducible here. Line 258-259 documents `includeTests: true`, which bb_patterns does not accept (engine-only option). Line 231 is milestone narrative (M57.T3); line 252 is 'the analyzer lane's work'; line 3 says 'bb_patterns reports code-pattern findings' without the text-surface limits. m16 D1 requires the lifecycle-method nuance (initialize/constructor can look unreferenced) that the page lost in an earlier rewrite; that leg is red and this page owns it.
defects.impact: The hand page is the tool's reference and it claims evidence not present, an option not offered, and process history instead of timeless facts.
defects.fixPlan: rewrite with the §8 header; move engine/report facts under a clear 'engine report vs tool answer' split; restore the lifecycle-method limitation as a plain fact; state that the corpus numbers were measured outside this checkout; delete includeTests as a tool option; remove milestone/lane narrative; keep verified gate counts (22/22, 29/29) and the known upstream failure.

defects.title: Descriptor has no machine-readable defaults or numeric bounds, and its one-line description overclaims 'evidence-derived' ranking for fixed-confidence classes
defects.observed: No property carries default/minimum/maximum even though src/mcp/tools/types.ts documents them for exactly this purpose; limit's maximum is stated nowhere. 'ranked by evidence-derived confidence' is true of orphans and the anti-pattern formulas but framework findings are a fixed 0.6.
defects.impact: A client cannot read the contract without prose; the description is slightly stronger than the engine.
defects.fixPlan: add default/minimum/maximum to schema properties; state 'framework findings are a fixed 0.6' in the description or scope the claim.

defects.title: Monolith import residue in the split handler: 82 of 91 named imports unused
defects.observed: 82/91 named imports are unused; they load the graph/impact/edit/visualize/migration/analysis engines at handler import time. The residue is also what makes the m13-docs 'handler only routes orphaned + all' check red: the import block contains the strings 'quality' (testQuality) and 'architecture' in banned-adjacent comments.
defects.impact: Unnecessary startup work on every tool load; a doc gate reads the residue as a routing claim.
defects.fixPlan: trim to the eight used symbols; the banned process comments in the same block go with it (P-18).

defects.title: Text-format surface omits the engine's own truncation marker and a grammar edge
defects.observed: The engine marks rule findings past the display budget truncatedByDisplayLimit and BB_PATTERNS documents that flag, but the text answer renders those rows identically to in-budget rows. The all-scope header reads 'across no rule(s)' when every class is switched off.
defects.impact: A caller cannot tell an overflow row from a page row in the text surface; cosmetic wording defect on the zero case.
defects.fixPlan: mark overflow rows in the text, or scope the docs claim to the engine report; fix the empty-case wording.

defects.title: The tool page's Staleness gallery has no per-mode registration because the tool emits no JSON envelope — the generated sentence is accurate for the surface but the remediation is not (see P-08)
defects.observed: Page says 'Freshness applies to the tool's read output (no registered per-mode split)' — true. The remediation sentence is the false part (P-08).
defects.fixPlan: regenerated with the Lead's generator branch.
